questions.prompt: A user with the default settings runs `CREATE TABLE Employees (Id INT, Name NVARCHAR(100));` without naming a schema. What table is created?
options: `dbo.Employees`
`sys.Employees`
`master.Employees`
An error, because a schema is required
questions.explanation: `dbo` exists automatically in every database, and if you don't specify a schema SQL Server uses it.

questions.prompt: After `ALTER USER AppUser WITH DEFAULT_SCHEMA = Sales;`, `AppUser` runs `CREATE TABLE Orders (...)`. Where does the table go?
options: `dbo.Orders`
`AppUser.Orders`
`Sales.Orders`
It fails because `Orders` has no schema prefix
questions.explanation: Setting a default schema for a user makes unqualified new objects go into that schema automatically.

source.section: Set Default Schema for a User (Optional)

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson call custom schemas a major security talking point compared with putting everything in `dbo`?
options: Custom schemas encrypt their tables
You can grant or deny access per schema, such as `GRANT ... ON SCHEMA::Sales` and `DENY SELECT ON SCHEMA::HR`
Users can't see `dbo` at all
Custom schemas store data on a separate disk
questions.explanation: With only `dbo`, access to it often means access to everything. Custom schemas allow fine-grained control. Schemas are logical only, not physical storage.

questions.prompt: Can `Sales.Users` and `HR.Users` exist in the same database?
options: No, table names must be unique across the whole database
Only if one of them is a view
Only if they are in different filegroups
Yes, two schemas can have tables with the same name
questions.explanation: A schema is a logical container, so the schema-qualified names `Sales.Users` and `HR.Users` are different objects.

questions.prompt: You are building a multi-tenant SaaS where each customer needs strict isolation and separate backups. Databases or schemas?
options: Schemas, because they are lighter to manage
A separate database per customer
One schema per customer inside `dbo`
It makes no difference for isolation
questions.explanation: Use different databases for complete isolation (separate backups, security, tuning). Schemas suit one application with related modules on shared infrastructure.
